title: Breaking the Lock-in: Diversifying Text-to-Image Generation via Representation Modulation
claim: A lightweight representation-level intervention turns near-identical samples from a fixed prompt into visibly more varied ones at negligible cost.
layout: Wide banner, left-to-right: method module, then Original vs DAVE image strips
description: The crop shows only the bottom strip of a wide figure, on a pale blue rounded background. At left is a partial method diagram. It shows a 'Block ℓ' box with h^ℓ arrows, and a pink panel with a bar chart of power against spatial frequency band, low to high. A green DC bar is lowered, with the label 'Suppress DC components (μ^ℓ)'. A golden key icon sits at the panel's corner, and a footnote defines h^ℓ as the output of the ℓth Transformer block. At right are two triplets of train-in-snow photos. The 'Original' triplet has a grey-green border, and its three views are very similar. The 'DAVE (Ours)' triplet has an orange border, and its views differ more in color, lighting and viewpoint. The eye goes first to the vivid orange DAVE images.
caption: Overview of DAVE. Compared to the original flow-based generative model, DAVE consistently produces more diverse images with minimal computation.
abstract: Recent text-to-image models built on large-scale Transformer backbones and flow-based objectives deliver strong text-image alignment and high visual quality, yet often produce overly similar samples under a fixed prompt. Existing diversity-enhancement methods alleviate this issue, but typically require expensive sampling or auxiliary optimization, incurring non-trivial overhead. To investigate the root cause of this homogeneity, we examine intermediate Transformer features and observe that the zero-frequency spatial average (DC) component rapidly converges across seeds early in generation, causing early trajectory lock-in that limits downstream variation. Building on this observation, we propose DC Attenuation for diVersity Enhancement (DAVE), a training-free representation-level intervention that selectively attenuates this component in the early regime. DAVE preserves the sampling pipeline with negligible overhead, improving prompt-consistent diversity while maintaining competitive image quality.
